title: How to encourage your baby's language development at home
subtitle: Small everyday actions can naturally support language growth.
summary: Simple daily actions can naturally support language development.

content.text: Language begins long before the first words appear. Your baby listens to voices, recognizes tones, and learns to connect sounds with people, objects, and emotions.
Talk during daily activities
You can describe what you are doing while dressing them, preparing their food, or going for a walk. You do not need to turn every moment into a lesson; just speak in a close and natural way.
Speak slowly, use simple phrases, and give them time to respond with sounds, gestures, or looks.
Read short stories
Books with large images and brief text are a great opportunity to point at objects, repeat sounds, and create special routines together.

items: Point to the drawings while naming them.
Repeat the words that catch their interest.
Let them touch and explore the book.
Do not worry about finishing the whole story.

content.text: What matters most is not teaching many words, but creating moments of connection around language.
Celebrate their attempts
When your baby tries to say a word, respond with enthusiasm and repeat it correctly without pressure. Every attempt is part of the process and can become a precious memory to keep in Hi Emi.

title: Complementary feeding: first steps
subtitle: A simple guide to support this new stage with calm.
summary: Practical ideas to begin this stage in a positive, calm, and safe way.

content.text: Complementary feeding is a stage of exploration. Flavors, textures, and colors are new for your baby, so patience is as important as the foods you offer.
Start with small amounts
Offer small portions and watch for hunger and fullness cues. It is not necessary for them to finish everything on the plate.
Check with your pediatrician before starting complementary feeding and whenever you have questions about allergies or specific foods.
Let them explore
Touching, smelling, and squishing food is also part of learning. Even if it gets messy, these experiences help your baby become familiar with food.

title: Sleep routines for calmer nights
subtitle: Simple habits to prepare a restful environment.
summary: Simple habits that can help you prepare a comfortable environment before bedtime.

content.text: A predictable routine can help your baby recognize that it is time to rest.
Repeat a simple sequence

items: Change the diaper and put on pajamas.
Speak softly or sing a song.

content.text: Every baby is different. Adapt the routine to your family's needs and consult a professional if difficulties continue.

title: Simple play ideas to spark curiosity
subtitle: Everyday activities to explore sounds, textures, and movement.
summary: Everyday activities to explore sounds, textures, colors, and movement.

content.text: Play is one of the main ways babies learn about the world. You do not need expensive toys to create meaningful experiences.
Explore safe household objects
Plastic containers, wooden spoons, and fabrics with different textures can become exploration tools under supervision.
Always stay close during play and avoid small parts, sharp edges, or objects that may pose a risk.
